title: Model-route percentile explorer: streaming vs non-streaming and tail isolation
creator: Priya Rao
description: Build an interactive explorer that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency percentiles per model + route, with an explicit breakdown between streaming and non-streaming (sync) request paths. This ticket covers backend aggregation, tracing hook tagging, metric/log pipeline adjustments, and the Grafana/Console UI panel. The goal is to make tail behavior and mode-specific regressions visible to SREs and platform/eng owners so rollouts and routing policies can be tuned quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Grafana/Console panel shows p50, p95, p99 for any selected model and route over arbitrary time windows
Panel provides a streaming vs non-streaming toggle (separate series) and stacked breakdown option
Each percentile point links to a trace sample (via trace id) or a trace-sample histogram for the tail bucket
Backend aggregates are computed at 1m and 5m rollups with correct percentiles and documented error bounds
Instrumented tracing adds 'io.mode' tag (values: 'stream'|'sync') and 'model.route' tag for correlation
No more than 5% additional overhead on median request path from new tracing tags in production (verified by perf run)
Dashboard supports filtering by region, serving pool (dedicated/hosted/private), and model variant
Playbook entry added describing how to use the explorer during incidents and to validate rollouts
tasks: Add 'io.mode' span tag in runtime for streaming path (ENG runtime change)
Emit model.route label on metrics pipeline at ingest producer for all request types
Update metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTLP) to calculate p50/p95/p99 per (model, route, io.mode) with 1m/5m rollups
Create Grafana dashboard panel and Console-integrated view with toggle and trace links
Backfill correctness verification job to compare streaming-tagged percentiles vs legacy aggregated metric
Run load/perf test to validate tracing overhead and metric cardinality impact
Documentation: add PRD + usage playbook + runbook snippets (Confluence)
comments: 2026-02-21 — Priya Rao: Initial kickoff notes. We need both a short-term panel that uses existing aggregates for fast visibility and a longer-term, low-cardinality pipeline to avoid metric explosion when we add io.mode. Proposed owner: Observability Core team.

2026-02-26 — Jonas Meyer: Scoped tasks and estimate (8). Decided approach: tag traces and metrics at producer side (runtime) to reduce downstream join complexity. Trade-off: slight increase in metric labels vs. much simpler query in Grafana.

2026-03-02 — Aisha Patel (SRE review): Request that we include region and serving_pool as optional filters. Also flagged need for a guard to drop high-cardinality model.variant labels for public hosted routes to limit Prometheus series count.
2026-03-04 — Jonas Meyer: Implemented runtime tracing tag change in PR runtime#6122 (link above). Added unit tests to verify tag presence for both streaming and sync code paths.

2026-03-06 — Priya Rao: Metrics pipeline prototype landed in platform#4256. Pipeline currently computes percentiles using HDR histograms; we need to document percentile error and rollup semantics (1m/5m).
2026-03-08 — Design feedback from Liam Chen: Visual distinction suggestion — use dashed lines for streaming series and solid for sync; also add a per-route sparkline for quick trend spotting.

2026-03-10 — Jonas Meyer: Load test results attached to PR show ~2% median latency increase when enabling span tags at p95 payloads; cardinality projection estimated +12% series. Planning a sampling knob if production impact exceeds threshold.

2026-03-12 — Priya Rao: QA smoke pass of Grafana panel completed. Trace linking works but we saw a few traces missing model.route tag for legacy clients — added a migration task to populate route using request headers when tag absent.

2026-03-12 — Customer Impact Note: This panel will help identify regressions seen in recent customer reports where p99 increased after a canary. Use panel to choose fallback model/route during incidents.
notes: Design decision: use HDR histograms for percentile compute in the ingestion pipeline to allow fast rollups; alternative was t-digest but HDR's fixed-bin approach gives more predictable error bounds at tails
Mitigation: if cardinality grows beyond projections, we'll enable 1) sampling for low-volume models, 2) aggregate fallback where io.mode='unknown' is merged with sync
Future work: add automated anomaly detection (regression alerts) scoped to model-route pairs with streaming/sync split
